system_response: A compact composite bow let mounted archers shoot without abandoning movement
evidence: May identifies the mobile horse-archer and composite bow as the center of pre-firearm steppe warfare.
limits: The synthesis does not provide one range accuracy or lethality value across periods.

military_problem: Disrupt a formed enemy without accepting its preferred fight
system_response: Feigned retreat and encirclement turned mobility into positional advantage
evidence: May treats feigned retreat and encirclement as standard tactical factors alongside weapons and armor.
limits: A tactical repertoire is not evidence that every army executed it successfully.

military_problem: Keep riders and scouts moving after a ridden horse tired
system_response: Spare horses spread work across a mobile herd
evidence: Martin cites Meng Hong's report that Mongol soldiers could have six or seven spare horses.
limits: This is a reported upper allowance not a universal average or an endurance calculation.

military_problem: Find enemies and protect dispersed columns before concentration
system_response: Scouts screened the army and reported conditions ahead
evidence: May describes scouts operating ahead and on the flanks of separate Mongol columns before concentration.
limits: The source does not quantify detection time information quality or a causal share of victory.
